question: Is there a wattage maximum for this cord?

question: Does this french press brew loose leaf tea well?

question: how far does this zoom (i'm a newbie) How far does this zoom?
answer: Most people, especially newbies, get a better feel for zoom magnification by comparing a digital lens ratio to the old 35mm standard. In this case, assuming you are using the 55-250 on something in the Digital Rebel series, the maximum zoom of 250mm compares to about 400mm on a 35mm film camera, which is considered a "long zoom" lens. Your 18-55mm kit lens has a maximum 35mm equivelent of about 90mm--perfect for portraiture, and about 1/4 the maxium magnification of the 55-250. (I'm rounding off everything here.) This is about the maxium zoom that you can hand-hold, assuming bright conditions allow a fast shutter speed and image stabilization (IS) is turned on. A tripod would typically be needed for anything longer than a digital 250mm, and anything longer than 150mm when conditions are less than optimum. So, for maxium zoom with minimal hassle, the 55-250mm IS is, in my opinion, the most effective Canon zoom for the price.

question: Xbox 360 compatibility issues: Why can't I download a game on my Xbox and be able to switch inputs and watch TV while it's downloading?

The older model elite and pro versions of the Xbox have some major issues with this receiver. The only way to avoid HDMI handshake issues is to run the HDMI from the Xbox straight to the TV and then run an optical audio cable to the receiver (this is not a bad solution neccesarily bc the Xbox can only output 5.1 audio as is the limitation for an optical audio cable - 7.1 is a PS3 thing bc it is HDMI 1.3a and Xbox 1.2) Anyhoo, I noticed that people with the new Slim Xbox's weren't having this problem. I went to the Xbox forums and found that with the old Xbox's this is a known problem and cannot be fixed. So I got a new Xbox Slim with Kinect. Before hooking it up, I found that the "BD" HDMI slot is the only one with HDMI Passthrough which helps a lot with HDMI handshake issues (this receiver has a 1.4 slot and the Xbox a 1.2 even the new Slim is 1.2). Now I have no problems whatsoever with Netflix movies cutting out or any other issues. So the only resolution is to get a newer model Xbox (Slim). Hope this helps and I wish someone would have been there to tell me that a long time ago to save me a lot of time

question: Can you resize recipes?
answer: Yes, Marilyn, you can resize recipes... it's called "scaling recipes" under the "help" section of MC 8. It can be done in several places, but most common is when you're in the "edit recipe" mode. Here's the instructions as given by MC 8: Recipe Scaling scales individual ingredients to change the total quantity produced by the recipe. MasterCook lets you input your own number of servings and your computer will adjust the ingredient amounts appropriately. This will often come in handy, but note that for a variety of reasons related to food chemistry, some recipes simply will not turn out the way the recipe author intended when you scale them. Souffls and other delicate foods are nearly impossible to scale. Some culinary experts warn against scaling complex recipes by more than a factor of two and against scaling recipes for baked goods at all. But for those recipes that can be scaled: To scale a recipe: 1. There are many areas and situations where the Scale feature is activated. The screen where you'll probably use the Scale feature most often is the Recipe Edit screen. 2. Click the Scale Recipe icon on the toolbar. 3. A box appears prompting you to enter a new number of servings. 4. Type in a new serving size and click OK. The ingredient amounts are adjusted to accommodate the new number of servings. In addition, the measurement units are also changed where appropriate. The cooking time and pan size are not adjusted. Hot Tip: Scaling affects only items in the Amount column. Be sure to check values such as pan sizes and cooking times which will need to be adjusted manually. 2004 ValuSoft, a division of THQ Inc. All Rights Reserved.

question: Will I still be able to use this TV after Feb 19, 2009??
answer: From everything I've researched, the answer to your question is yes. It has an ATSC/NTSC tuner that lets you enjoy over-the-air analog and digital TV broadcasts. Also, here is an excerpt in FAQs from www.dtv.gov (http://www.dtv.gov/consumercorner.html#faq7). How can I be sure that I am buying a digital TV (DTV)? By law, beginning March 1, 2007, all television reception devices (including TVs, VCRs, DVRs, etc.) imported into the U.S. or shipped in interstate commerce must contain a digital tuner. Retailers may continue to sell analog-only devices from existing inventory, but must prominently display on or near the analog-only device a Consumer Alert label with this advisory: CONSUMER ALERT This television receiver has only an analog broadcast tuner and will require a converter box after February 17, 2009, to receive over-the-air broadcasts with an antenna because of the Nation's transition to digital broadcasting. Analog-only TVs should continue to work as before with cable and satellite TV services, gaming consoles, VCRs, DVD players, and similar products. question: is there one item to id gemstones and what is it?
answer: No one item alone will positively identify a colored gemstone since many synthetics have the same optical, chemical, and physical properties of natural stones. Generally, it is a combination of different instruments that help in identification, and then that needs to be coupled with experience in separating some synthetics from natural. A refractometer will give you the refractive index of a gemstone, and in some cases that can serve as a positive ID if no true synthetic has been produced for that particular stone. But even then, the r.i. of some gemstones overlap each other, as well as being the same color, which makes other testing necessary.

question: My garbage disposal doesnt have a hole underneath to stick the jambuster into. so what now?

Assuming that doesn't work, kill the circuit to the disposer. Then use the oldest method in the books. Stick a broom handle down in side and lever it around and around, reversing direction. Use a flashlight to look inside for things like glass or flatware and carefully fish them out. Rinse only if the water is flowing through. Try and fire it up! If you hear nothing but a click, which can happen at the same moment as the switch clicks so it is easy to miss, the breaker may pop again. Try it all a few times before ordering a new one! Good luck!

question: It seems like a change was made to fix the "deep sleep" issue. If you bought between 9/2013 and 12/2013, how are things going?
answer: After dealing with an HP inkjet fax in my restaurant that kept jamming and having dried up ink from, I decided I needed a compact laser that would fit in the allocated area.This fit the bill, except that it was white and every other piece of equipment in the area was black. Once I unboxed the unit, I used masking tape to cover the black areas and any open electronics. Using a simple flat black can of spray paint, I was able to make it all black. Nobody can tell it was painted even when I point it out to them. First problem fixed. I have had the unit for about 7 months and it has performed flawlessly. It even uses the same toner as a wireless Brother printer I have which is a bonus as well. This past week of course, I encountered the DEEP SLEEP curse that so many people speak of. The machine will do half a ring and act weird, but will not receive faxes. After some research and playing around, there is a solution, even though Brother has decided to hide the feature. You ARE able to disable DEEP SLEEP. Go to General Settings, Ecology, Sleep Mode. When it asks you to change the time before sleep, simultaneously press the START and DOWN ARROW buttons. You will now get the hidden option to Disable DEEP SLEEP mode. Disable it and enjoy your fax for many years to come.

question: What material is used for fire retardant? Are there any chemical off gas from this mattress? Thanks.
answer: This is what I found online about soy foam which is what is in this mattress along with the latex. But I would suggest you google it also to see what you can find on the subject. "The current market is in a craze over soy-foam. Marketed as being better for the environment than polyurethane based foams, we did some research to see what this 'green' foam was all about. As it turns out, Soy foam is not much better than poly-based foam, and some people would argue that it has the same impact. Soy foam is actually made the same way as the polyurethane based foam, with 20% of the mixture being replaced as soy product. So the foam is 20% soy, 33% isocyanates, and 47% polyurethane.? Due to the polyurethane content, the foam still requires the toxic flame retardants, and the foam contains the same level of isocyanates. Currently, soy foam also biodegrades at the same rate as poly-based foam. The reason for the low percentage of soy content is that when soy is present at higher levels it produces an undesirable, burnt smell. In addition, the use of pesticides and fertilizers on the soy crop have a negative impact on the environment, as do the mono cultures in which soy is planted. Soy is such a diverse and valuable food source that it may not be used best as a plastic substitute."

question: Can it be used for monitoring tire pressure in realtime/every few seconds pressure reading - for R&D test purposes? Thank you
answer: The answer to your question is "No, the sensors cannot be used for high frequency real time pressure monitoring." While it is correct that the display cycles through each tire configured with a sensor, every few seconds, in fact the readings do not change that frequently. In order to extend the life of the sensors' batteries, each sensor emits its readings by radio frequency transmission to the monitor/display roughly every 5 minutes. (Those emissions occur asynchronously from one another.) The one exception to that reporting scheme occurs if the sensor detects a rapid reduction in pressure, such as would occur in a blowout. Then it reports immediately, and the monitor alarms immediately. This behavior of the sensors is clearly evident when the monitor is first turned on. Initially, the monitor cycles through the tires, but no readings are displayed. As any given sensor reports, then the next time it's turn comes up in the display cycle the values (pressure and temperature) will be displayed. After a few minutes many of the sensor values are populated, but it may take as long as 5 minutes to receive a reading from all the sensors. The 5 minutes is not in the specs, as far as I can see, but was told to me by the sales rep. It seems about right from casual observation. It could be timed precisely by turning off the monitor immediately after a reading for a particular tire is first reported, then turning it back on and timing how long it takes to reappear. I have observed that when a sensor stops reporting, such as due to marginal rf transmission conditions, the monitor will wait until it is overdue in reporting then will signal with a single beep, not with the alarm that occurs for exceeding a limit or rapid tire deflation. (I can monitor from inside my house but at times the sensor farthest from the display will drop out and a beep will sound each time that tire is to be displayed by the monitor.)

question: HD Mino Freezes - Reboot doesn't work: Anyone else out there have a similar problem?
answer: I have had my Mino HD for a few months and while recording have often had it freeze up. Usually I have been able to reset it by holding the power on button or plugging it into USB, but today that didn't work. I searched around the internet and the answer posted below which came from Flip support appears to have resolved my problem as well: "had the same problem when it was brand new straight out of the box. Below is Pure Digital's (manufacturer of the Mino HD) response. This did solved my problem. "Please ensure that you are gently touching the operational buttons on the camcorder rather than pressing them. Pressing too hard, or too rapidly in succession while waiting for a response, can desensitize the touch pad, requiring a reset of the camcorder. If you find that the Mino has already frozen, we suggest resetting the camcorder. To reset, simply take a pin and insert it into the reset hole within the camera's tripod mount, wait five seconds before powering on, and then power on without touching any of the buttons on the back of the camcorder for an additional five seconds. Please note that resetting the camcorder in this manner will not affect the videos resident on the camcorder; it will simply reset the screen and button sensitivity on the Mino. Thank you, Flip Video Support" I hope this helps. BTW my Mino HD has frozen twice now (I've had it for 2 hours total so far!) and the reset trick has fixed it both times. It seems to me the buttons are too sensitive or the computer program not the most stable. I hope this is the last of the problems! "

question: The first time I placed the pellets in the microwave, a number of them turned blue; however, after approximately 2-3 minutes they were gray again. Wh
answer: It is extremely unlikely that your Super Dri-Aid is faulty. What you are describing is a situation which requires additional drying cycles. When rejuvenating (drying) exhausted Super Dri-Aid pellets using a Microwave oven set to the recommended 1/2 power at 30 Second intervals one must keep in mind that all Microwave ovens are not created equal and power output varies from unit to unit. The guidelines provided are designed to allow you to safely dry Super Dri-Aid in most any microwave oven. After a few drying cycles are performed in one microwave, another unit may require some an additional cycles to provide the same results since the power output level may differ. As heat is applied the moisture evaporates and the indicator pellets turn from neutral gray to blue indicating that the adsorbed moisture is being removed and the pellets are dry ready to use. However, if the blue starts to fade to neutral gray after a few minutes, it is an indication that they require additional 30 second cycles to thoroughly remove additional moisture which is especially prevalent in very humid climates. Once drying is completed the pellets should be placed back into its original jar and closed tightly until ready to use.

question: Sir, My capacitor has three wires , h-compressor , f&c- to motor which two do I use . Thank`s, John
answer: What is your question? What type of AC unit do you have, i.e., RV roof unit, portable unit, floor unit, wall unit, commercial roof unit? Every capacitor is different based on it schematic drawing located inside cover plate. I will assume you have a RV 13,500 BTU AC unit. If so, take the cover off the air conditioner unit of your travel trailer. Open the access panel. Look at the schematic drawing on the access panel or ac cover. The brown wire is for the fan of the ac unit, do not install to the brown wire. The hard start capacitor black wire that has extra connector at the end is connected to red line and the other black wire is connected to the yellow wire of the ac unit. The instructions that came with the hard start capacitor should show which black line with the extra connector connects to the red line and the other goes to the yellow line.

question: Will this power 10 3W 700ma Leds in Series? Would this one be good enough or should I buy the 24V version? Can this also power 10 5W leds 1500ma leds?
answer: No. Based on info provided doing some quick math a 3 watt 700 mA Led would have a voltage drop (3W/.7 amps) of about 4.285 volts per Led. using 3 LEDs in series would give total drop across all three about 12 volts. If you notice the LED strips are sets of 3 LEDs in series with a current limiting resistor in series with each set of 3 LEDs, not all LEDs just in series. Answer is: no neither one would work. If you connected the LEDs correctly then this power supply would work for either as both ten 5 watt and ten 3 watt LEDs are both less then the 60 watts. All the LED strips I've seen can be cut into sets of 3 LEDs or cut at any length of 3 sets, it might be easier to buy a cheap LED strip and cut off what ever amount of LED sets you need as they are already connected with current limiting resistors and only need to be connected to a 12V power supply of correct wattage. if must have ten LEDs in series then you would need to calculate for that... ten 3 watt LEDs would need about a 43 volt power supply and would still need a current limiting resistor in series too. Good luck on finding a 43 volt power supply... most likely would need to use a 48 volt supply and calculate voltage drop and limiting resistor values

question: will this hold spinning rods? Does that mean keeping the reel facing up (upside down) on the unit?
answer: It will hold spinners in the proper position (reel down). There is a notch on the underside of the holder for the reels base to enter (under the opening where the rod slides in). However, some spinning reels might have a base that is too wide to actually lock in. Of course the opening could be widened with a dremel or something if a better fit is needed. I have a spinner that doesn't quite lock in but since there is a twist ring to hold the butt of the rod a little better, it's not a huge issue. I also use tethers on my rods in the event I roll my kayak or a fish pulls it out of the holder so I don't need it to be held only by the rod holder. Another issue is if you have rods with really long butts, is that the butt may stick out the back too far and hit your boat (in my case a kayak). When that happens, you need to change the angle so that everything fits correctly. I would highly recommend playing with the arrangement before you actually mount the rod holder. Put your equipment in the holder, check angles and mount points and ensure that it will work for what you want to do. They are very versatile but prior planning is the key. This is likely not a big issue if you're on a larger boat with tons of space. Hope that helps.

question: Does this use a lot of data? City vs Highway, is there a big difference in data usage?
answer: I have unlimited Data with my Verizon plan, but honestly the greatest amount of Data used by cell-phone maps is the map itself. Since I cannot even get the local map to pull up with GPS signal alone, unless I have my data connection turned on, I assume that my Android-based phone waits and downloads the map information through Google-maps live, on the fly, and only stores a small amount of whatever is near me through the route calculated to my stated destination. I actually think it too bad the user does not have the Option with Android to retain all map data once it is downloaded, perhaps up to a certain volume (200MB maybe?) and allow the live feed to simply 'correct' whatever is newer as it comes in. I would seldom miss the live Traffic info that colors the route green-yellow-red on my google navigation. When in the Cobra-App, it is just like having your Navigator in MAP mode (no routing or navigation shown). The amount of extra data to download the live user-reported risk areas from Cobra would be insignificant next to that. So if you are already using your phone for navigation, you should have 'about' the same level of data usage, regardless. I will say that I have found it particularly useful having a live download of stationary camera locations. Drivers have to be extra-vigilant around red-light intersections and speed-watches, since camera-tickets are notoriously inaccurate and occasionally found programmed to maximize the profit of the company getting a kick-back based on how many tickets are generated, rather than truly penalizing only the reckless drivers. On having a Radar Detector in every car: My state puts up construction signs with radar onboard, which results in an audible and flashing alert to watch carefully that you are at the correct speed for every Construction zone. You REALLY don't want to accidentally be cruising into one of those at 65 mph.

question: [Q] Recommendation for Wifi Router to share USB 1TB HDD: Would appreciate if somebody can share his/her experience sharing usb hdd over local wifi network.
answer: Any storage you attach to a wi fi router will be very slow, especially compared to wired links. There are several reasons for this but the most important one is a router is designed to make sure no one link/channel sucks up the entire bandwidth that is available. If you had a "business" router you could establish rules that would let you work around this but consumer models are made to be "user friendly". You *might* be able to tweak the "game" settings to allow greater throughput but then you would have to set up your storage programs to use certain ports. IMO you are better off using wired LANs (and/or one of the four Ethernet ports on the router) for heavy duty storage transfers. However, this unit will do just fine if all you need are routine backups (especially at night) and nominal file access by a few users. I have 1TB attached through the USB port and another 2TB attached via wireless and while transfers are slow they are acceptable for home use. Note that USB is going to be the slowest of all choices with a router, behind wi fi (a bit faster) and ethernet (very fast).

Eventually there will be a software update for the TV that allows the Vizio remote to connect over your home wifi network so that it no longer requires line of sight to work. You can also get a small accessory known as an IR blaster which would sit on your media console or closer to your tv and other components. It receives the IR signals from your remotes and repeats them at an angle/location that will be more likely to get to the TV.

question: What are the functional differences among X32 Full, Compact and Rack?
answer: From what I can tell, it is the physical knobs for each of the controls. Also when I did the research I was looking at the Compact and the Producer, and they only had 16 XLR input channels and from what I could tell, you had to purchase the S16 digital snake. I opted for the full board as everything is available right in front of you and there are less "layers" that you have to scroll through (IE on the Compact or Producer I believe that you have 4 separate buttons with 8 channels each and with the full board you only have 2 buttons with 16 channels each. I am no doubt a professional yet, but I wanted to learn on a full board with as much in front of me as possible and that why i chose this. Was it right, that I do not know but i LOVE the board and so does the band that I mix for. On the rack mount version - I really know nothing about it. I would assume that its the same and maybe controlled by the X32 control software available. The large board hooked up perfect to my DAW (Studio One) and connected pretty easy with my MAC. I ran into a little trouble with the LAN because I connected a wireless router to a wireless router, but after I figured this out it works like a champ. Another reason I went with the X32 versus digital boards is how many youtube videos I could find on training. Excellent selection - many of which are from Church perspectives but its a band they are mixing - and usually have more to deal with than straight mixing music. Hopefully that is a little explanation - but if I was to spend the money for the Compact, Producer or the Full board, hands down I would purchase it again. While it might be $100-1500 difference, the full board for me works great.

The motor usually will turn at this reduced voltage, but with a loss of power and torque.
